storyTagline: One more title in green, then the coach walked out the door and the league traded everything that wasn't nailed down.

stories.headline: The Last Dance in New York
stories.dek: The Jets went 15-2, beat the Eagles in Super Bowl CXLI and handed Dorren Skura his 57th title. Then the coach took the keys to Atlanta.

stories.headline: Atlanta Calling, Then the Shuffle
stories.dek: The coach took three champions south and kept two. When the trades stopped, the Falcons were Heath, London, Maxwell and Woodrum, and The Ox was a Bear.

stories.headline: Champions Nobody Recognizes
stories.dek: The Jets kept the trophy. The coach, the MVP, the Super Bowl MVP and the Offensive Player of the Year all left. This is who is left to defend it.

stories.headline: Three Quarterbacks, Three New Homes
stories.dek: The Super Bowl MVP is a Giant, the Ravens' starter now runs the champions' offense, and Drake Wise was a Falcon for exactly one trade.

stories.headline: The Ox and Starscream
stories.dek: Kane Van Oxley played his way into the S tier. Vyncint Heath played his way onto the map in 17 games.

stories.headline: The Other Side of the Ledger
stories.dek: Not every stock went up. Two veteran receivers lost their bite and the market cooled on two defenders.

stories.headline: Record Watch: Jensen Closes In
stories.dek: Trequan Jensen is one big season from Rondale Ikarras. The tackles race has a new name in it.

stories.headline: Milestones: 50,000, 2,500 and a 7th Ring
stories.dek: Kirk Lenoir joined the 50,000-yard club, Ward Jr joined the Hall of Fame, and Jakeem Friend kept collecting jewelry.

stories.headline: Same Opponent, Different Uniform
stories.dek: Three Super Bowls against the Eagles, three wins, with three different clubs.

stories.headline: Where Are They Now: The Ones Who Walked
stories.dek: Alvin Tufele retired, Dylan Hyatt left the league and Blair Iupati never played a down in green.

vault.text: Some defensive linemen are measured in sacks. Zander Kolar was measured in tackles. Career Legacy 9,119, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Wayne Wilson
vault.text: Four hundred thirty-one games. Nobody in this league has played longer. Career Legacy 8,933, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lukas Russell
vault.text: The Running Man started fast and never slowed down. Career Legacy 8,827, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jayon Queen
vault.text: Two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Only one other player in this league has ever matched that. Career Legacy 8,747, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Nick Bolton
vault.text: One of the originals, and he never stopped tackling. Career Legacy 8,634, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jahmyr Gibbs
vault.text: Mr. Incredible was here at the start, and he set the bar high. Career Legacy 8,573, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ray Waller
vault.text: Never count out a man whose nickname is a promise. Career Legacy 8,443, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Bilal Tolbert
vault.text: No individual trophies. Four rings. And a sack record nobody has caught. Career Legacy 8,366, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyrone Baugh
vault.text: Seven seasons, seven championships, and Tyrone Baugh has a ring for every one of them. Career Legacy 8,353, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lloyd Queen
vault.text: Some linemen hunt quarterbacks. Lloyd Queen hunted everybody else. Career Legacy 8,056, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Mose Junior
vault.text: Some players chase rings. Mose Junior chased ball carriers. Career Legacy 7,752, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Amani Bryant
vault.text: The best quarterback never to win a ring. Career Legacy 7,751, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lamar Jackson
vault.text: The league never had to explain who he was. He was just Him. Career Legacy 7,654, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyler Pacheco
vault.text: Tyler Pacheco never needed the big play. He needed the ball, and he got it. Career Legacy 7,352, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Akiem Bouye
vault.text: Akiem the Dream was there at the beginning. Career Legacy 7,345, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cooper Dean
vault.text: The best offensive lineman in the league never needed a highlight. He just needed a man in front of him. Career Legacy 7,070, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Michael Wilson
vault.text: Wayne's brother, and nobody's afterthought. Career Legacy 8,314, Y79 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Dan Mosley
vault.text: 2,658 tackles from a defensive back. Read that again. Career Legacy 7,710, Y79 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Kyric McQuay
vault.text: Twice in three seasons Ray Waller reached the Super Bowl and lost. Kyric McQuay was the reason both times. Career Legacy 7,201, Y79 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jakeem Friend
vault.text: Linemen do not win trophies. Jakeem Friend won seven rings instead. Career Legacy 11,384, Y80 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jason Macleone
vault.text: One look at Scary Jerry and you understood the name. Career Legacy 7,536, Y80 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Taron Hayes
vault.text: Twice the league looked at every defender in football and picked Taron Hayes. Career Legacy 7,154, Y80 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Forrest Everett
vault.text: Hand Forrest Everett the ball near the goal line and send the kicking team out for the extra point. Career Legacy 7,111, Y80 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Pharoah Hunter
vault.text: The other receiver in the Vikings dynasty was never anybody's second option. Career Legacy 7,529, Y80 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Abraham Ward Jr
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game, every game, for 236 games. Career Legacy 7,530, Y82 class.
